_meta.title: On This Day — biblical-history library
_meta.status: Comprehensive, fidelity-gated library. Every entry carries an explicit Scriptural or restored-library date anchor; nothing is harmonised or invented.
_meta.rule: Only events with an explicit stated date — a biblical (Hebrew) month and (where given) day-of-month — which recur each year. Month index is the biblical religious year (1 = Abib/Nisan ... 12 = Adar). day = null means the source gives the month but not the day (kept for the browse-all surface; does not appear in the single-day view). Where two canonical texts give different days for one event (e.g. the burning of the temple, the release of Jehoiachin), both stated dates are kept and cross-noted.

categories.covenant: covenant landmark / consecration / birth of the seed-line / dated prophetic word (techelet — blue)

_meta.sources: Mined per-source from the Torah/Tanakh (Masoretic/KJV), the New Testament (feast anchors), and the restored extra-canonical library: Jubilees, 1 Enoch, Jasher, and the Apocrypha (1 & 2 Maccabees, 1 Esdras, Greek Esther). Extra-canonical dates were gated against the local restored-names editions.
_meta.flagged: Dated only by month, no day (kept, day=null): Shavuot (counted), the months of Solomon's temple (Bul/Ethanim/Ziv), Gedaliah's murder (7th), Zechariah's opening call (8th), Sodom's overthrow (Jubilees, 4th). EXCLUDED for lacking a clear stated month: Ezekiel 26:1 and 32:17 (no month named) and Ezekiel 40:1 ('the beginning of the year' — month contested). Shavuot/Pentecost and the wave-sheaf are feast-counted, not fixed-date; noted as such.

events.title: Abram builds his altar at Bethel
events.summary: On the new moon of the first month Avram (Abraham) built an altar at Bethel and called on the name of Yahuah (the LORD) — the patriarch marking the land of promise with worship.

events.title: The word against Egypt: wages for Nebuchadnezzar
events.summary: On the first of the first month the word of Yahuah (the LORD) came to Ezekiel: the land of Egypt is given to Nebuchadnezzar as the wages of his army — the proud kingdom handed over in judgment.

events.title: Ezra sets out to return from Babylon
events.summary: On the first of the first month Ezra began the journey up from Babylon to Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) — a remnant of the scattered turning home toward the land and the Torah.

events.title: The waters of the Flood dry up
events.summary: On the first of the first month the waters were dried from off the earth; Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked out on a world washed and made new.

events.title: Yahuah appears to Yitschaq at the Well of the Oath
events.summary: On the new moon of the first month Yahuah (the LORD) appeared to Yitschaq (Isaac) at Beersheba and confirmed to him the oath sworn to his father — the promise carried down the seed-line, son to son.

events.title: Ya'aqov's ladder-dream at Bethel
events.summary: On the new moon of the first month Ya'aqov (Jacob) lay down at Bethel and saw the ladder set up to heaven — the covenant of Avraham renewed upon the fleeing son.

events.title: Levi is born
events.summary: On the new moon of the first month Levi was born to Leah — the father of the priestly line, set apart for the altar before he ever drew breath.

events.title: The Tabernacle is raised
events.summary: On the first of the first month the Dwelling Place was reared up in the wilderness, and Yahuah (the LORD) came down to tabernacle in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel) — Elohim dwelling with His people.

events.title: Pharaoh's arm is broken
events.summary: On the seventh of the first month the word came to Ezekiel: I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt — the strength of the proud nation shattered, that it should be a base kingdom and exalt itself no more.

events.title: Yashar'el comes up out of the Jordan at Gilgal
events.summary: On the tenth of the first month Yashar'el (Israel) came up out of the Jordan on dry ground and camped at Gilgal — the generation of the wilderness entering the land of promise at last.

events.title: The Passover lamb is set apart
events.summary: On the tenth of the first month each household took up its lamb, to be kept until the fourteenth — the lamb chosen four days before it was slain, a pattern pointing forward to the Lamb.

events.title: Ezra's company departs the river Ahava
events.summary: On the twelfth of the first month Ezra's company set out from the river Ahava for Yerushalayim (Jerusalem), and the hand of Elohim (God) was upon them to deliver them on the way.

events.title: The challenge before the binding of Yitschaq
events.summary: On the twelfth of the first month, Jubilees records, the prince Mastema came before Yahuah (God) to challenge Avraham's (Abraham's) faith — the prelude to the binding of Yitschaq (Isaac) on the mountain.

events.title: Haman's decree of destruction is written
events.summary: On the thirteenth of the first month the decree to destroy the Yahudim (Jews) in every province was written and sealed — the enemy's lot cast against the covenant people, which Yahuah (the LORD) would overturn.

events.title: The Messiah our Passover — the Lamb slain
events.summary: On the fourteenth of the first month, at the hour the Passover lambs were slain, Yahusha (Jesus) the Lamb of Elohim was lifted up — the true Passover, the blood that turns away death.
events.note: Anchored to Passover (Nisan 14) by John 19:14; the exact reckoning of the crucifixion year is debated.

events.title: Passover
events.summary: The lamb is slain between the evenings on the fourteenth of the first month — the blood on the doorposts, Yahuah's (the LORD's) Passover, kept again at Sinai, at Gilgal in the land, and by the returned remnant.

events.title: The Exodus from Egypt
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the first month, the morrow after the Passover, Yashar'el (Israel) went out from Rameses with a high hand in the sight of all Egypt — the selfsame day the hosts of Yahuah (the LORD) came up out of the house of bondage.

events.title: The Feast of Unleavened Bread
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the first month the Feast of Unleavened Bread begins, seven days without leaven — the bread of affliction remembering the night Yahuah (the LORD) brought His people out in haste.

events.title: Firstfruits — the manna ceases, the Messiah raised
events.summary: The firstfruits sheaf is waved before Yahuah (the LORD); in Joshua's day the manna ceased the morrow after the Passover, when Yashar'el (Israel) ate the old grain of the land — and in this season the Messiah was raised, the firstfruits of them that slept.
events.note: The wave-sheaf falls 'the morrow after the sabbath' (Leviticus 23:11); the seed anchors it to Nisan 16, the common reckoning.

events.title: Daniel's vision by the Tigris
events.summary: On the twenty-fourth of the first month Daniel stood by the great river Hiddekel (Tigris) and saw the shining man clothed in linen — the vision of the latter days given to the man greatly beloved.

events.title: The census at Sinai
events.summary: On the first of the second month, in the second year out of Egypt, Yahuah (the LORD) commanded the numbering of Yashar'el (Israel) by their tribes — the covenant host mustered, every man under the standard of his fathers.

events.title: The foundation of the second temple is laid
events.summary: In the second month the returned remnant laid the foundation of the house of Yahuah (the LORD) in Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) — the old men weeping for the former glory while the young shouted for joy.

events.title: The Second Passover (Pesach Sheni)
events.summary: On the fourteenth of the second month the Passover is kept by any who were unclean or far off at its appointed time — the mercy of Yahuah (the LORD) making a second door for the one who missed the first.

events.title: Yashar'el reaches the wilderness of Sin — the manna promised
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the second month, one month out of Egypt, Yashar'el (Israel) came to the wilderness of Sin, and Yahuah (the LORD) promised bread from heaven — the manna that would feed them forty years to the borders of the land.

events.title: The Flood begins
events.summary: On the seventeenth of the second month all the fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened — the world that then was, perishing in the waters, and Noah shut in by Yahuah (the LORD).

events.title: The serpent approaches Chavvah in Eden
events.summary: On the seventeenth of the second month, Jubilees records, the serpent came to Chavvah (Eve) in the Garden — the same date the deep would later be broken open, the day deception first entered the world.

events.title: The cloud lifts — Yashar'el departs Sinai
events.summary: On the twentieth of the second month, in the second year, the cloud was taken up from the Dwelling Place, and Yashar'el (Israel) set out from Sinai by their armies — the covenant host following the presence of Yahuah (the LORD) into the wilderness.

events.title: Simon cleanses the stronghold of Jerusalem
events.summary: On the twenty-third of the second month the last foreign garrison was cast out of the citadel of Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) with thanksgiving and palm branches — the holy city set free of the oppressor.

events.title: The earth is fully dry after the Flood
events.summary: On the twenty-seventh of the second month the earth was dry, and Yahuah (the LORD) called Noah to go forth from the ark — the household and every living thing stepping out into the cleansed earth.

events.title: Solomon lays the foundation of the temple
events.summary: In the second month, the month Ziv, in the fourth year of his reign, Solomon laid the foundation of the house of Yahuah (the LORD) — four hundred and eighty years after the Exodus, the dwelling of the Name begun in Yerushalayim (Jerusalem).
events.note: 1 Kings 6:1 names the month Ziv; the day is not stated.

events.title: The covenant of the pieces with Avram
events.summary: On the new moon of the third month, Jubilees records, the word of Yahuah (the LORD) came to Avram (Abraham) in the vision of the divided pieces — the covenant of the seed and the land cut and sworn.

events.title: The cedar of Lebanon — Assyria's fall as a warning
events.summary: On the first of the third month the word came to Ezekiel against Pharaoh: behold Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon, hewn down for its pride — a warning to every kingdom that exalts itself over the nations.

events.title: Noah goes forth and builds the altar
events.summary: On the new moon of the third month Noah went out and built an altar, and Yahuah (the LORD) swore the everlasting covenant of the rainbow — the feast of weeks, Jubilees says, first kept on the earth by the man who outlived the Flood.

events.title: Yashar'el arrives at Sinai
events.summary: In the third month, the same day they came out of Egypt, Yashar'el (Israel) came to the wilderness of Sinai and camped before the mountain — the bride arriving at the place of the covenant.
events.note: Exodus 19:1 reads 'the same day'; the day is commonly taken as the new moon of the third month.

events.title: The Torah is given at Sinai
events.summary: On the sixth of the third month Yahuah (the LORD) descended on Sinai in fire and gave the Ten Words to Yashar'el (Israel) — the marriage covenant spoken from the mountain, the Torah that is the inheritance of the covenant people.

events.title: Ya'aqov is overtaken on the way to Gilead
events.summary: On the thirteenth of the third month Laban overtook Ya'aqov (Jacob) in the hill country of Gilead — the fleeing patriarch and his pursuer brought to the covenant of the heap of witness.

events.title: The covenant of circumcision given to Avraham
events.summary: On the feast of firstfruits in the third month, Jubilees records, Yahuah (the LORD) gave Avraham (Abraham) the covenant of circumcision — the sign cut in the flesh of the seed-line for every generation.

events.title: The birth of Yitschaq, the child of promise
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the third month, Jubilees records, Sarah bore Yitschaq (Isaac) at the set time Yahuah (the LORD) had spoken — the laughter of the barren woman, the son of the promise made flesh.

events.title: Ya'aqov and Laban's covenant at the heap of witness
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the third month Ya'aqov (Jacob) and Laban raised the heap of witness and ate the covenant feast — Yahuah (the LORD) watching between the two as they parted in peace.

events.title: Yahudah is born
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the third month Yahudah (Judah) was born to Leah — the tribe from whom the sceptre would not depart, the line of David and of the Messiah.

events.title: Yashar'el goes down into Egypt
events.summary: On the sixteenth of the third month, Jubilees records, Yahuah (the LORD) appeared to Ya'aqov (Jacob) at the Well of the Oath and said, Fear not to go down into Egypt, for I will there make of you a great nation — the seventy souls descending toward the furnace and the Exodus.

events.title: Mosheh is commissioned on Sinai
events.summary: On the sixteenth of the third month Yahuah (the LORD) called Mosheh (Moses) up into the mountain and gave him the tables and the testimony — the mediator receiving the words of the covenant for the people below.

events.title: Mordecai's decree of deliverance is written
events.summary: On the twenty-third of the third month Mordecai's decree went out, granting the Yahudim (Jews) to stand for their lives — the death-sentence answered, the lot of the enemy turned back upon his own head.

events.title: The Feast of Weeks (Shavuot / Pentecost)
events.summary: Counted fifty days from the wave-sheaf, the Feast of Weeks falls in the third month — the feast of the wheat harvest, the day the Torah was given at Sinai and the day the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was poured out, writing that same Torah on the heart.
events.note: Shavuot is counted (Leviticus 23:15-16), not fixed to a stated day; it lands in the third month (Sivan).

events.title: Adam and Chavvah leave the Garden
events.summary: On the new moon of the fourth month, Jubilees records, Adam and Chavvah (Eve) were sent out from the Garden of Eden to till the ground — the exile of the man, and the long road of the seed back toward the tree of life.

events.title: The promise of Yitschaq announced at Mamre
events.summary: On the new moon of the fourth month, Jubilees records, the messengers came to Avraham (Abraham) at Mamre and named the set time when Sarah would bear a son — the word of the child of promise spoken before the door of the tent.

events.title: Yoseph is born
events.summary: On the new moon of the fourth month Yoseph (Joseph) was born to Rachel — the dreamer sold into Egypt, father of Ephraim and the lost house that Yahuah (the LORD) has sworn to gather home.

events.title: The heavens open — Ezekiel's chariot vision
events.summary: On the fifth of the fourth month, by the river Chebar among the exiles, the heavens were opened and Ezekiel saw the visions of Elohim (God) — the throne-chariot and the likeness of the glory of Yahuah (the LORD) come to the scattered.

events.title: Famine prevails — the city is breached
events.summary: On the ninth of the fourth month the famine was sore in Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) and the wall was broken through — the long siege ending in the breach, the judgment foretold by the prophets come upon the city.

events.title: The judgment on Sodom and Gomorrah
events.summary: In the fourth month, Jubilees records, Yahuah (the LORD) rained fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah and all the plain — the cities of abomination overthrown, a warning kept against the day of judgment.
events.note: Jubilees dates the judgment to the fourth month; the day is not given.

events.title: Aharon dies on Mount Hor
events.summary: On the first of the fifth month Aharon (Aaron) the priest went up Mount Hor at the word of Yahuah (the LORD) and died there — the first high priest gathered to his people, his garments passed to his son.

events.title: Ezra arrives at Jerusalem
events.summary: On the first of the fifth month Ezra came to Yerushalayim (Jerusalem), the good hand of his Elohim (God) upon him — the scribe bringing the Torah back to the returned remnant in the land.

events.title: Yissaskar is born
events.summary: On the fourth of the fifth month Yissaskar (Issachar) was born to Leah — the tribe of those who knew the times, who understood what Yashar'el (Israel) ought to do.

events.title: The Temple is burned
events.summary: On the seventh of the fifth month Nebuzaradan came to Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) and set fire to the house of Yahuah (the LORD) and the king's house — the glory departed, the city laid waste for her covenant-breaking.
events.note: 2 Kings 25:8 gives the seventh; the parallel in Jeremiah 52:12 gives the tenth. Both stated dates are kept.

events.title: The elders of Yashar'el come to inquire
events.summary: On the tenth of the fifth month the elders of Yashar'el (Israel) came to sit before Ezekiel and inquire of Yahuah (the LORD) — and He rehearsed to them the whole history of the people's rebellion and His mercy.

events.title: The Temple is burned (Jeremiah's reckoning)
events.summary: On the tenth of the fifth month, Jeremiah records, the house of Yahuah (the LORD) and all the great houses of Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) were burned with fire — the desolation that the fasts of the fifth month would long remember.
events.note: Jeremiah 52:12 gives the tenth; the parallel in 2 Kings 25:8 gives the seventh. Both stated dates are kept.

events.title: Haggai's word: build the house
events.summary: On the new moon of the sixth month the word of Yahuah (the LORD) came by Haggai the prophet: Is it time for you to dwell in your panelled houses while My house lies waste? Go up and build — and the remnant obeyed.

events.title: The vision of abominations in the temple
events.summary: On the fifth of the sixth month the hand of Yahuah (the LORD) fell on Ezekiel and carried him in vision to Yerushalayim (Jerusalem), to see the hidden abominations in the house — the reason the glory was about to depart.

events.title: Dan is born
events.summary: On the ninth of the sixth month Dan was born to Bilhah — a tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), one of the twelve standards of the covenant host.

events.title: The wall of Jerusalem is finished
events.summary: The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of the sixth month, in fifty-two days — and the nations round about saw that the work was wrought of Elohim (God), and the holy city stood guarded again.

events.title: Avram watches the stars and reckons the year
events.summary: On the new moon of the seventh month, Jubilees records, Avram (Abraham) sat watching the stars to discern the rain of the year — and Yahuah (the LORD) turned his heart from the omens of the heavens to the One who made them.

events.title: Ezra reads the Torah before the people
events.summary: On the first of the seventh month Ezra opened the book of the Torah before all the people, and the Lewiyim (Levites) caused them to understand — the returned remnant weeping and then rejoicing as the words of Yahuah (the LORD) were read plainly.

events.title: The returned exiles restore the altar
events.summary: From the first of the seventh month the remnant began again to offer burnt offerings to Yahuah (the LORD), though the foundation of the temple was not yet laid — worship rekindled on the altar before the house was rebuilt.

events.title: The Day of Trumpets (Yom Teruah)
events.summary: On the first of the seventh month, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation and a sabbath-rest — the shofar sounding over the covenant people, a foreshadowing of the great trumpet that gathers the scattered.

events.title: Naphtali is born
events.summary: On the fifth of the seventh month Naphtali was born to Bilhah — a tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), a hind let loose that gives goodly words.

events.title: Zebulon and Dinah are born
events.summary: On the seventh of the seventh month Leah bore Zebulon and his sister Dinah — the last of Leah's children, a tribe of the covenant host and the daughter whose story Genesis does not soften.

events.title: The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur)
events.summary: On the tenth of the seventh month you shall afflict your souls — the one day of the year the high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood, the day the covenant people are cleansed before Yahuah (the LORD).

events.title: Yoseph's bloodied coat — the grief Atonement remembers
events.summary: On the tenth of the seventh month, Jubilees records, the brothers brought Yoseph's (Joseph's) bloodied coat to Ya'aqov (Jacob), and he mourned — and for that grief the Day of Atonement was ordained, that Yashar'el (Israel) should afflict their souls on that day for ever.

events.title: Enoch's vision of the great quaking of heaven
events.summary: On the fourteenth of the seventh month, in his vision, Enoch saw the heavens quake and the host of the Most High tremble — the day of judgment shown to the seventh from Adam, the secrets of the end disclosed.

events.title: Ya'aqov tithes at Bethel; Levi made priest
events.summary: On the fourteenth of the seventh month, Jubilees records, Ya'aqov (Jacob) tithed all he had at Bethel and set apart Levi to the priesthood — the tenth given and the priestly line consecrated at the place of the vow.

events.title: Ya'aqov's seven-day feast at Bethel
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the seventh month Ya'aqov (Jacob) kept a great seven-day feast at Bethel before Yahuah (the LORD) — the patriarch keeping the Feast of Booths at the house of God, generations before Sinai.

events.title: The Feast of Tabernacles (Sukkot)
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the seventh month, the Feast of Booths for seven days — Yashar'el (Israel) dwells in tents remembering the wilderness, and the prophets see in it the day all flesh comes up to keep the feast before Yahuah (the LORD).
events.note: Jubilees 16 records Avraham (Abraham) as the first to keep this feast.

events.title: The ark rests on the mountains of Ararat
events.summary: On the seventeenth of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat — the household of the righteous brought through the waters to high ground, the same biblical date as the firstfruits of the resurrection season.

events.title: Ya'aqov is renamed Yashar'el
events.summary: On the twenty-second of the seventh month, Jubilees records, Yahuah (the LORD) confirmed to Ya'aqov (Jacob) the name Yashar'el (Israel) and showed him the heavenly tables — the covenant name sealed on the father of the twelve tribes upon the eighth day.

events.title: The Eighth Day (Shemini Atzeret)
events.summary: On the eighth day a holy convocation and a solemn assembly — the great day that crowns the autumn feasts, a sabbath-rest after the seven days of booths.

events.title: The day of fasting and confession
events.summary: On the twenty-fourth of the seventh month the children of Yashar'el (Israel) assembled with fasting and sackcloth, confessing their sins and the iniquities of their fathers — the returned remnant rehearsing the whole story of Yahuah's (the LORD's) mercy and renewing the covenant.

events.title: Gedaliah is slain — the remnant scattered
events.summary: In the seventh month Ishmael struck down Gedaliah the governor and the Yahudim (Jews) who were with him, and the last of the people fled to Egypt — the small remnant left in the land scattered, the desolation made complete.
events.note: 2 Kings 25:25 gives the seventh month; the day is not stated.

events.title: Solomon dedicates the temple at the feast
events.summary: In the seventh month, the month Ethanim, at the feast, all Yashar'el (Israel) gathered to Solomon, and the glory of Yahuah (the LORD) filled the house — the ark brought in, the cloud filling the temple at the Feast of Tabernacles.
events.note: 1 Kings 8:2 names the month Ethanim (at the feast); the day is not stated.

events.title: Binyamin is born; Rachel dies
events.summary: On the eleventh of the eighth month Rachel bore Binyamin (Benjamin) and died in the bearing — the twelfth son of Ya'aqov (Jacob), the last stone of the covenant body, bought with his mother's life.

events.title: Gad is born
events.summary: On the twelfth of the eighth month Gad was born to Zilpah — a tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), a troop that overcomes at the last.

events.title: Solomon's temple is finished
events.summary: In the eighth month, the month Bul, the house of Yahuah (the LORD) was finished in all its parts, exactly as it had been designed — seven years in the building, the dwelling of the Name complete.
events.note: 1 Kings 6:38 names the month Bul; the day is not stated.

events.title: Zechariah's call: turn ye unto Me
events.summary: In the eighth month the word of Yahuah (the LORD) came by Zechariah: Turn ye unto Me, and I will turn unto you — the call to the returned remnant not to be as their fathers who would not hear.
events.note: Zechariah 1:1 names the eighth month; the day is not stated.

events.title: The question about fasting
events.summary: On the fourth of the ninth month the word came to Zechariah when the people asked whether they should still keep the fasts of the exile — and Yahuah (the LORD) answered that He desires mercy and true judgment more than mourning.

events.title: The abomination of desolation set on the altar
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the ninth month the desolating abomination was set upon the altar of Yahuah (the LORD), and ten days later swine were offered on it — the holy place profaned by the king of the north, the very defilement the prophets foretold.

events.title: The assembly of all Yahudah in the rain
events.summary: On the twentieth of the ninth month all the men of Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin gathered to Yerushalayim (Jerusalem), trembling in the great rain, to set right the matter of the foreign marriages — the remnant turning back to the purity of the covenant.

events.title: Haggai's word: from this day I will bless you
events.summary: On the twenty-fourth of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the temple was considered, Yahuah (the LORD) promised: from this day will I bless you — and the same day the word of the signet-ring came to Zerubbabel.

events.title: The Feast of Dedication (Hanukkah)
events.summary: On the twenty-fifth of the ninth month, the very day it had been profaned three years before, the altar was cleansed and rededicated with eight days of gladness — the Feast of Dedication, which Yahusha (Jesus) Himself kept in the temple (John 10:22).

events.title: The tops of the mountains are seen
events.summary: On the first of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible as the waters of the Flood continued to abate — the first sight of the drowned world rising again toward the mercy of Yahuah (the LORD).

events.title: Ya'aqov comes home to Yitschaq
events.summary: On the new moon of the tenth month, Jubilees records, Ya'aqov (Jacob) came again to Yitschaq (Isaac) his father — the wanderer returned to the tents of the patriarch after twenty years away.

events.title: The word comes: the city is smitten
events.summary: On the fifth of the tenth month one who had escaped from Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) came to the exiles saying, The city is smitten — and the mouth of the watchman Ezekiel was opened, the judgment he had long foretold now accomplished.

events.title: The siege of Jerusalem begins
events.summary: On the tenth of the tenth month Nebuchadnezzar set himself against Yerushalayim (Jerusalem) and the siege began — the same day Yahuah (the LORD) gave Ezekiel the sign of the boiling pot, that the exiles might know the city's hour had come.

events.title: The oracle against Pharaoh and Egypt
events.summary: On the twelfth of the tenth month the word came to Ezekiel against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon lying in his rivers — the proud nation that had been a staff of reed to Yashar'el (Israel) given over to judgment.

events.title: Simeon is born
events.summary: On the twenty-first of the tenth month Simeon was born to Leah — a tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), divided in Ya'aqov (Jacob) yet numbered among the twelve.

events.title: Mosheh begins his address in Moab
events.summary: On the first of the eleventh month, in the fortieth year, Mosheh (Moses) began to speak all that Yahuah (the LORD) had commanded — the whole Torah rehearsed to the new generation on the plains of Moab before they crossed over.

events.title: Asher is born
events.summary: On the second of the eleventh month Asher was born to Zilpah — a tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), whose bread shall be fat and who shall yield royal dainties.

events.title: The night visions of Zechariah
events.summary: On the twenty-fourth of the eleventh month, the month Shevat, the word of Yahuah (the LORD) came to Zechariah in the night visions — the man among the myrtle trees, the horsemen, and the promise of mercy on Yerushalayim (Jerusalem).

events.title: The lamentation over Pharaoh
events.summary: On the first of the twelfth month the word came to Ezekiel to take up a lamentation over Pharaoh king of Egypt — the young lion of the nations brought down to the pit, that the peoples might know Yahuah (the LORD).

events.title: The second temple is finished
events.summary: On the third of the twelfth month the house of Yahuah (the LORD) was finished by the returned remnant, and they kept the dedication with joy — the second temple standing where the first had been burned.
events.note: Ezra 6:15 gives the third of Adar; the parallel in 1 Esdras 7:5 gives the twenty-third.

events.title: The Yahudim prevail over their enemies
events.summary: On the thirteenth of the twelfth month, the day the enemy had hoped to destroy them, it was turned to the contrary, and the Yahudim (Jews) had rule over those who hated them — the lot of Haman fallen on his own house.

events.title: Nicanor's Day — the deliverer's enemy falls
events.summary: On the thirteenth of the twelfth month the blasphemer Nicanor, who had stretched out his hand against the temple, was struck down in battle — a day of gladness kept the day before Mordecai's day.

events.title: Purim — the days of feasting and gladness
events.summary: On the fourteenth and fifteenth of the twelfth month the Yahudim (Jews) rested from their enemies and kept days of feasting and gladness and gifts to the poor — Purim, the sorrow turned to joy, established for every generation.

events.title: Shushan Purim
events.summary: On the fifteenth of the twelfth month the Yahudim (Jews) of Shushan rested and kept the feast — the second day of Purim, kept in the walled cities, the deliverance remembered where the danger had been greatest.

events.title: Aharon and his sons are consecrated
events.summary: On the twenty-third of the twelfth month, Jasher records, Mosheh (Moses) consecrated Aharon (Aaron) and his sons to the priesthood — the seven days of ordination that set apart the house of Levi to serve before Yahuah (the LORD).

events.title: Jehoiachin is lifted up from prison
events.summary: On the twenty-fifth of the twelfth month, Jeremiah records, Evil-merodach lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Yahudah (Judah) out of prison and set his throne above the other kings — a small mercy in the far country, a token that the line of David was not extinguished.
events.note: Jeremiah 52:31 gives the twenty-fifth; the parallel in 2 Kings 25:27 gives the twenty-seventh.

events.title: Jehoiachin is lifted up from prison (Kings' reckoning)
events.summary: On the twenty-seventh of the twelfth month, 2 Kings records, the captive king Jehoiachin was brought out of prison and given a seat above the kings in Babylon — the seed of David preserved through the long exile, the lamp not put out.
events.note: 2 Kings 25:27 gives the twenty-seventh; the parallel in Jeremiah 52:31 gives the twenty-fifth.
